title: Ternary operators and logical operations
concept: Concise condition expression with the ternary operator (?:), short-circuit evaluation of && and ||

steps.title: Starting the main function and initializing variables
steps.explanation: **`int age = 20;`** and **`int has_id = 1;`** — two integer variables are created in the stack frame. `age` is age (20), `has_id` is whether you have an ID card (1 = yes).

steps.title: Conditional assignment with ternary operator
steps.explanation: **`char *status = (age >= 18) ? "Adult" : "Minor";`** — **The Ternary Operator** condenses if-else into **just one line**.

steps.title: status output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Status: %s\n", status);`** — `%s` is a string placeholder. Reads `"Adult"` indicated by `status` and outputs `Status: Adult`.

steps.title: && (logical AND) - both conditions are true
steps.explanation: **`if (age >= 18 && has_id) {`** — The **`&&` (logical AND)** operator is entirely true only if both conditions are **both true**. `20 >= 18`(true) && `has_id`(1, true) → Since it is true, the if block is executed.

steps.title: AND condition passed - Entry allowed output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Entry allowed\n");`** — Since both conditions are true, `"Entry allowed"` is printed. This condition is expressed in code: “You must be 18 years or older and have an ID card to enter.”

steps.title: || (logical OR) shortened evaluation
steps.explanation: **`int result = (age > 0) || (10 / 0);`** — `||` (logical OR) is true if **any one thing** is true. However, `(10 / 0)` is division by 0, so the program **crash** when executed!

steps.title: Output and end shortened evaluation results
steps.explanation: **`printf("Short-circuit: %d\n", result);`** — `result = 1` is printed. Thanks to shortened evaluation, division by zero is completely avoided.

quiz.explanation:
|| The operator does not evaluate the right side if the left side is true (shorthand evaluation).
Since x = 5, (x > 0) is true. So func() is not called.
If x = -1, (x > 0) is false, so func() is executed.

misconceptions.wrong: && and || always evaluate to both sides
misconceptions.correct: Logical operators in C have short-circuit evaluation. Once the result is confirmed, the rest is ignored.
misconceptions.why: This is because the entirety of && is confirmed to be false if the left side is false, and the entirety of || is confirmed to be true if the left side is true.

keyTakeaway: The ternary operator provides concise condition expression, and the shortened evaluation of &&/|| creates safe code by skipping unnecessary operations.
